subject: Post-demo: unit economics deep-dive & model-split confirmation
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
To: Samantha Ruiz <samantha@kuratech.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 15 Sep 2028 14:03:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo: unit economics deep-dive & model-split confirmation

Hi Samantha — great to connect today, thanks for the thoughtful product walkthrough. Per our chat, I wanted to capture the unit-econ calibration and the model-mix assumptions so we can align on a practical quote and the mutual action plan. Please see a short summary + asks below.

Quick summary of what we heard from KuraTech (please correct anything):
- Intended first-phase volume: ~15M tokens/month (initial canary).
- 12-month ramp target: 100–120M tokens/month.
- High-level budget range: $9k–$12k/month initially (you said this is flexible with demonstrated quality/latency).
- Primary workload breakdown: recommender + similarity + lightweight chat for UX flows.

My proposed framing and specific asks:
1) Target $/1M tokens you want us to aim for: you mentioned ~$600–$800/1M in our call. Can you confirm final target (we'll use this to draft a pricing scenario)?
2) Model mix (we sketched this live). Please confirm split you expect month 1 vs month 12:
   - Month 1 suggested: embeddings 45%, chat 50%, rerank 5%
   - Month 12 suggested: embeddings 55%, chat 40%, rerank 5%
3) Canary plan: start with 2–4 week canary at ~15M tokens/mo equivalent traffic pattern (we can set an ops window and throttles). Are you open to a 30% credit on the first month if we meet the latency/quality gates?
4) Procurement and SLA ask: are SOC 2 + standard SLA (99.9% uptime) sufficient or do you need a custom SLA/contract language?

Preliminary unit-econ scenarios (high-level):
- Scenario A (self-serve hosted): $900/1M tokens => 15M = $13,500/mo; 100M = $90,000/mo
- Scenario B (committed dedicated + 12-mo): $650/1M tokens => 15M = $9,750/mo; 100M = $65,000/mo
(These are illustrative — I will run exact math with Sales Ops once you confirm target $/1M and the month-1 split.)

Next steps (what I need from you):
- Confirm the target $/1M token range to use for proposal (one number or a small band).
- Confirm the month-1 model split you actually expect to send traffic for.
- Share any compliance requirements (SOC 2 evidence, IP/data residency notes) so I can include in the quote.

Attachments: I can share a short pricing workbook and a sample mutual action plan once we lock the numbers (will attach in follow-up).

Thanks — I’ll hold off on involving Sales Ops until you give the go-ahead to shop the committed-tier pricing.

—
Karthik Iyer
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
karthik@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0123

Thanks Samantha — this is super helpful and matches what we heard in the demo. A few clarifications and a concrete plan to move to quote: 

1) Pricing scenarios mapped to your numbers (quick math):
   - If we price at $800/1M: 15M => $12,000/mo; 120M => $96,000/mo.
   - If we price at $650/1M (committed): 15M => $9,750/mo; 120M => $78,000/mo.

   Note: the committed/dedicated option assumes a 12-mo commit and allows us to offer lower unit price and guaranteed capacity for your heavier embedding workloads.

2) Model-routing recommendation (initial):
   - Route embeddings to an embed-optimized instance (lower per-token cost, higher throughput).
   - Route chat to the standard chat pool with a small LRU cache for common completions.
   - Keep rerank on a dedicated small batch lane to reduce latency spikes.

3) Canary & credit: we can do a 2–4 week canary at ~15M tokens/mo. I will propose a promotional credit for month 1; need Marissa/Sales Ops OK to lock the percent.

Next steps (I will do):
- With your confirmation on the $/1M target, I’ll send our pricing workbook (rough worksheet attached).
- With approval, I’ll loop in Sales Ops to build two formal quotes (hosted vs committed dedicated).
- We will propose a 30-day mutual action plan with milestones (connect infra, SOC 2 evidence, sign PO).

Please let me know if you want me to include a preliminary SLAs addendum.

—
Karthik
